main_text.head: EXERC. XVIII.
AN PARTIS SIMILARIS FORMA aliquo morbo laborare possit?
main_text.p: PRiusquam ad formæ partis similaris morbos progrediar, quid appellatione formæ (ne ulli homonymia imponat) Fernelius nobis significatum voluit, paucis expediam. Primũ ipse libro de Differentijs morborum formam partis similaris appellat totam substantiam: ubi quoq; totius substantiæ nomine insitum spiritū, illius diuinum calorem, & facultates aitse complecti.Deinde libro de Abditis rerum causis secundo, ipsam formam alias essentiam uocat, & partium similarium speciē: alias totam rei substantiam, quam quidem perfectionem esse & integritatem, qua res unaquæq; consistit, mox exprimit.Cap.7.Quibus locis omnibus quid sibi uelit Fernelius, nomine formæ, uix percipi potest. Veruntamen quantum hæc inter se discrepant, saepe nobis conuenit. Forma in primis non esse rei totam substantiam aperte demonstrat Aristoteles libro secundo, de Anima, ubi ex triplici genere naturalis substantiæ tres differentias colligit. Dicimus (inquit)

page.notes: Marginal notes at right: "Cap.7." beside the first paragraph and "Cap.9." beside the second paragraph line ("caufis" / "Abditis rerum"). The second is partly cut off and reads as printed "Cap.9.". Several words in the body are doubtful due to the faded scan, especially "ipse", "insitum spiritū", "aitse", "uix", "saepe", and the Aristotle passage ("ex triplici genere"); these should be checked. The text as printed contains "Cap.7." and "Cap.9." as marginal references, and I have placed the second one as a note at its line. Final line "F 2 (inquit)" is a signature mark with the catchword-like word "(inquit)" in the text.
